units.title: Self-dependence
units.intro: Grammar: the main parts of speech (nouns, pronouns, verbs, adjectives) and basic punctuation (full stop, question mark, exclamation mark, comma).

cards.title: Parts of speech (1)
rule: A **noun** names a person, place, thing or idea (*teacher, Keren, book, freedom*). A **pronoun** replaces a noun (*he, she, it, they, him, them*). A **verb** shows an action or state (*run, is, seem*). An **adjective** describes a noun (*a **hard-working** student*).
The same word can be different parts of speech: *a **work** of art* (noun) / *They **work** hard* (verb).

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: The scholarship committee awarded the funding to Aster and ________ after reviewing our academic portfolios.

steps.text: The pronoun follows the preposition 'to' and forms part of a compound prepositional object ('to Aster and [pronoun]').
This slot requires the objective case ($$\text{Preposition} + \text{Object Pronoun}$$).
Students often write 'Aster and I' because 'Aster and I' is common in the subject position.

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: The old typewriter in the headmaster's office is still functional, but ________ keys are difficult to press.

steps.text: The blank modifies the noun 'keys' to show ownership.
Students often confuse 'its' (possessive adjective) with 'it's' (contraction of 'it is' or 'it has').

cards.title: Punctuation (1)
rule: **Full stop (.)** ends a statement. **Question mark (?)** ends a direct question. **Exclamation mark (!)** shows strong feeling. **Comma (,)** separates items in a list, and follows an introductory word or clause: *However, ...*; *When I arrived, ...*

examples.text: I bought rice, sugar, oil and salt.

cards.title: Unit summary
body: Nouns name things, pronouns replace nouns, verbs show actions or states, adjectives describe nouns. End statements with a full stop, questions with a question mark, strong feelings with an exclamation mark; use commas in lists and after introductory words.
